result.title: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning
result.summary: We study how the layers in deep neural networks (NNs) converge, using Wilsonian Renormalization-Group (RG) ideas to organize the spectral picture. During training, these layers often develop heavy-tailed power-law (PL) spectra, and the strongest checkpoints often appear near the PL exponent $α\approx 2$. This pattern raises a simple question: why should this value mark a well-trained layer? The answer is both statistical and physical. Our statistical hypothesis is that $α=2$ marks the boundary between stable if not optimal learning and overfitting via non-self-averaging. The physical answer is that the same value makes the spectral energy gain scale evenly across logarithmic spectral scales, which is the proposed Wilsonian marginal condition. We then apply the ERG trace-log condition, the proposed SETOL theory, which we justify by taking volume-preserving, scale-invariant transformations to remove arbitrary layer scale along the proposed RG flow. The resulting spectral RG flow connects the HTSR and SETOL theories to optimizers such as Muon, and motivates a new optimizer extension, WW-PGD. Together, these results point toward a spectral Renormalization-Group view of learning, in which NNs may approach shared spectral structure in the settings studied here.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用 Wilsonian 重整化群视角分析深层网络的层级收敛，指出训练中层权重谱常呈重尾幂律、且最优检查点附近幂律指数 α≈2，并从统计（过拟合与非自平均的边界）与物理（对数谱尺度上能量增益均匀，即 Wilsonian marginal 条件）两方面给出解释，进而提出 SETOL 与谱 RG 流，联系 HTSR、Muon 等优化器并给出新优化器 WW-PGD。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其谱幂律指数与尺度不变的重整化流可作为分析 LVR 内部状态表示几何与深度/训练阶段演化的诊断视角，可供核查是否对 latent 状态谱结构有解释力。
